component.name: Lightforge
component.summary: Install, update and play World of Warcraft on Linux, and a home for all your other Battle.net games

description.p: Lightforge is a native Linux launcher for World of Warcraft. It talks to Blizzard's content servers directly — the same TACT/CASC pipeline the real client uses — so it installs, patches, verifies and launches every flavour of WoW on its own, without Battle.net in the way.
Battle.net is still there if you want it: the launcher builds and maintains one Wine prefix for it, and everything you install through it gets a tile here too.

ul.li: Installs Retail, Classic, Classic Era and Anniversary, with their PTR and beta branches.
Resumes an interrupted download instead of starting it again.
Verifies an install two ways, and re-fetches only what is damaged.
Keeps games on as many drives as you like, and leaves installs it finds where they already are.
Downloads, checks and manages Proton-GE itself — no Steam, no Lutris, no system Wine.
Manages addons from CurseForge, WoWInterface, Tukui and GitHub in one list.
Per-game launch settings: CPU performance profile, MangoHud, Wayland backend, high-resolution textures and your own environment variables.

description.p: A bigger update, mostly stability and bug fixes from bug reports. Adds running two games at once, quitting Battle.net from Lightforge, moving a game to another drive, pre-downloads and a diagnostics page.

Fixes the Battle.net install on SteamOS and the Wine prefix hang on fresh setups. Adds a STOP button for running games, a Proton installer window, a rebuilt Game Settings window, and updating Lightforge from its own update notice.

A stability release built from bug reports: Battle.net and Scan & Repair no longer refuse to start because of leftover Proton processes, the display fits handhelds in Game Mode, Faugus installs are found, addons with third-party downloads disabled offer their GitHub release, and Settings has a cleaner look.

Full controller support for the Steam Deck and Steam Machine, a double-click installer, safer addon and Proton updates, backups of your WoW settings, and error messages that say how to fix the problem.
The WoW: Forever stress test can be pre-installed beside the beta, with a note under the button saying when its servers open, and WoW: Forever appears in Add a game.

An install found during setup is added even when its folder refuses new files, cancelling a download is possible at last, the Wine prefix is tidied the moment a game quits rather than on the next launch, and the launcher says when a newer release exists.
Play unlocks when the game closes rather than when the Wine prefix has finished winding down, and News on the Play page is off until you ask for it.
